title: Surgical egress throttling for GPU workloads — operational playbook
author: Priya Menon
body:
Overview:

This playbook describes surgical egress throttling patterns we use to protect multi-tenant GPU-serving capacity during network egress surges. It is intended for on-call infra, SREs supporting GPU pools, and platform engineers who operate egress proxies, NAT gateways, and Terraform modules that control tenant bandwidth and priorities.

Goals and scope:
- Maintain service availability for latency-sensitive inference workloads while containing egress cost and avoiding global network saturation.
- Provide a set of automated and manual mitigations that can be applied to individual tenants, tenant groups, or entire regions.
- Document Terraform and CI/CD patterns for rolling out throttling rules and testing them in lower environments.

When to use this playbook (trigger conditions):
1) System-level: total egress bytes/min by a region exceeds 85% of provisioned NAT/Egress capacity for 5m with sustained growth rate > 10%/5m.
2) GPU-pool impact: GPU tenant queue latency > SLO (95th percentile inference queuing > 200ms) and correlates with outbound bandwidth saturation.
3) Cost alert: burst egress spend acceleration exceeding forecasted daily budget threshold.

Key metrics to inspect (dashboards/queries):
- infra.egress.bytes_per_minute.{region} (rollup by tenant_tag)
- infra.egress.nat_queue_length
- gpu.pool.queue_latency_p95
- gpu.tenant.active_sessions and gpu.tenant.kv_cache_hit_rate
- egress-proxy.rate_limited_requests_by_tenant

SLOs and guardrails (policy):
- Per-tenant soft egress cap: 500 MB/min by default for shared GPU pools (configurable per tier).
- Per-tenant hard cap (emergency): 2 GB/min — requires manual approval or oncall action to raise.
- Regional NAT headroom: keep 20% free capacity for control-plane and system spike.
- Alert thresholds: trigger P0 when region egress > 95% for 3m and GPU-queue-latency_p95 >200ms.

First-responder checklist (fast path):
1) Confirm the alert: correlate egress and GPU metrics in the regional dashboard.
2) Identify top 5 tenants by egress volume (query: top_k(infra.egress.bytes, 5) grouped by tenant_tag).
3) Check recent deploys / eval jobs (CI/CD) that might have kicked off large downloads or dataset syncs.
4) If a single tenant is dominant (>40% of region volume), apply surgical throttling to that tenant (see Automated mitigations).
5) If multiple tenants drive load or a system burst, enable regional emergency throttling and shift non-critical tenants to the burst pool.

Automated mitigations (recommended order):
- Step A: Apply per-tenant rate-limit via egress-throttler service (preferred, surgical).
  - Command example (kubectl exec to control-plane pod):
    ```bash
    curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \n      -d '{"tenant":"tenant-123", "rate_bytes_per_min": 524288000}' \n      https://egress-control.internal/api/v1/tenants/rate-limit
    ```
  - Expected result: immediate reduction of outbound throughput for tenant within 30–60s.

- Step B: Apply NAT-level queue shaping (wide but quick).
  - Terraform toggle: flip `regional_nat_shaper.enabled = true` then `terraform apply -var region=us-west-2` (sample config below).
  - Use when several tenants are above their soft caps or when proxy instability is observed.

- Step C: Re-route non-latency-critical traffic to dedicated burst pool (fractional GPU / lower-priority pool).
  - Update routing rule in gateway: mark tenant_tag -> burst-subnet and adjust routing policy in router.

Manual mitigations and communication steps:
1) Post an incident note to #infra-oncall with summary and top offenders.
2) Notify Customer Success for affected high-tier customers if throttling will impact production.
3) If the offending tenant is running evals or large downloads, suggest they use the on-demand dataset mirror in the same region (internal URL).
4) If an emergency hard cap is applied to a paying customer, escalate to infra manager and account owner for approval.

Terraform / IaC example (egress-throttler module):
| Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|
| tenant_id | string | - | Tenant identifier to create a rate-limit policy for. |
| rate_bytes_per_min | number | 524288000 | Soft rate limit applied to tenant in bytes/min. |
| hard_cap_bytes_per_min | number | 2147483648 | Emergency hard cap that requires approval. |
| region | string | us-west-2 | Target region where rules are provisioned. |

Sample HCL snippet:
```hcl
module "egress_throttler_tenant_123" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo/internal-terraform-modules.git//egress-throttler"
  tenant_id = "tenant-123"
  rate_bytes_per_min = 524288000
  hard_cap_bytes_per_min = 2147483648
  region = var.region
}
```
CI/CD and test gate guidance:
- All changes to the throttler module must include: unit tests for Terraform plan diffs, an integration test that uses the staging egress-proxy mock to confirm traffic shaping works, and a rollback plan in the PR description.
- Local QA commands (run in the staging workspace):
  - make test-infra && TF_WORKSPACE=staging terraform plan -var-file=staging.tfvars
  - run the egress-proxy-load generator: `./tools/egress-load --tenant tenant-123 --rate 600MBm` and verify the throttler reduces throughput to ~500MB/min.

Runbook: how to apply a surgical throttle (operator steps):
1) Identify tenant id and confirm owner: `./scripts/tenant-lookup tenant-123` (returns contact and billing tier).
2) Apply soft throttle via egress-control API: POST as shown above.
3) Monitor metrics for 10 minutes, confirm region headroom and GPU queue latency improvement.
4) If no improvement, escalate to NAT-level shaping (Terraform).
5) Document action in incident: which tenant, rate applied, reason, and rollback criteria (e.g., latency back under SLO for 15m).

Rollback and recovery criteria:
- Rollback the throttle when:
  - regional egress utilization < 70% for 10m AND GPU queue latency_p95 < 150ms for 20m.
  - OR customer remediation confirms dataset jobs are re-scheduled into a low-cost mirror.
- How to rollback: reverse the API call (delete or set rate_bytes_per_min to tenant baseline) and `terraform apply` to restore NAT shaper config.

Operator safety and customer handling rules:
- Never apply hard caps to enterprise paying customers without contacting account owner.
- For automated throttling, annotate the tenant metadata with an incident id so Customer Success can follow up.
- Respect privacy: do not include file names or dataset contents in public incident channels.

Escalation matrix and ownership:
- Oncall infra: #infra-oncall (pager) — primary responder.
- GPU SRE oncall: pager (for queue/eviction impacts).
- Network platform: network-oncall@redwood.internal (for NAT/GW changes).
- Infra manager oncall (for hard-cap approvals): managers@redwood.internal

Playbook testing and exercises:
- Quarterly chaos test: simulate a tenant producing a 3x egress spike for 15m in staging; verify throttler, NAT shaping, and routing to burst pool.
- Game day checklist: confirm Terraform can roll forward and backward within 10 minutes in the staging workspace.

Table: alert -> immediate action mapping
| Alert | Severity | Immediate action | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Region egress >95% for 3m + GPU queue_p95>200ms | P0 | Apply region-level NAT shaper, notify #infra-oncall | infra oncall |
| Single tenant >40% region egress | P1 | Apply per-tenant soft throttle via egress API, contact tenant owner | infra oncall + platform |
| Unexpected egress spike from CI pipeline | P1 | Pause CI pipeline (rerun gate), apply throttle to CI service account | CI/CD team |

Post-incident items and postmortem template (required for P0/P1):
1) Timeline: sequence of detection, mitigation and recovery actions with timestamps.
2) Root cause: what triggered the egress spike.
3) Customer impact: list impacted tenants and severity.
4) Mitigations applied and why chosen.
5) Follow-ups: config changes, Terraform module improvements, automation opportunities.
6) Action owners and deadlines.

Implementation notes and improvements backlog (examples):
- Add dynamic per-tenant budgets that scale with tier and time-of-day.
- Better CI isolation: move heavy dataset downloads to mirrored storage in region.
- Expand throttler observability: percent of bytes dropped, per-tenancy latency tails after shaping.

Related pages and references:
- egress-proxy architecture doc (internal link)
- nat-shaper-operator README
- staging chaos harness runbook

Appendix: quick commands and snippets
- Query top tenants (Grafana/PromQL):
  `topk(5, sum(rate(infra_egress_bytes_total[1m])) by (tenant_tag))`
- Apply API throttle (curl example):
  `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"tenant":"tenant-123","rate_bytes_per_min":524288000}' https://egress-control.internal/api/v1/tenants/rate-limit`
- Terraform apply (staging):
  `TF_VAR_region=us-west-2 TF_WORKSPACE=staging terraform apply -var-file=staging.tfvars -target=module.egress_throttler_tenant_123`

This document is intended to be a living playbook; please update it after each exercise or incident.
